subject: math

objective.text: A whole is 2 halves, 3 thirds or 4 fourths. Find the missing parts to make a whole.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Describe a whole by the number of equal parts including 2 halves, 3 thirds, and 4 fourths.

explanations.title: Complete the whole
explanations.text: 1 half and 1 half make 1 whole. 3 thirds make 1 whole. 4 fourths make 1 whole.

explanations.title: Fewer parts, bigger pieces
explanations.text: Halves are the biggest pieces. Fourths are the smallest. Thirds are in the middle.

explanations.title: Draw the rest of the whole
explanations.text: This is 1 fourth. Draw 3 more fourths of the same size. Now there is 1 whole.

examples.title: Thirds of a rectangle
examples.text: 2 children hold 1 third each. That is 2 thirds. Add 1 more third. 3 thirds make 1 whole.

misconceptions.label: Thinking different numbers of parts cannot be equal wholes
misconceptions.description: Child thinks 2 halves and 3 thirds cannot be the same amount because the numbers differ.
detection_signals: Says 3 thirds is more than 2 halves because 3 is more than 2.
misconceptions.response_text: 2 halves make 1 whole. 3 thirds also make 1 whole. If the wholes are the same size, they are equal.
